name: SUMAC
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Aaron Turner set out to make the heaviest music of his life, found his drummer through Kurt Ballou, and then kept pulling the riffs apart until improvisation got in.

eras.title: Heavier than a bag of hammers
eras.text: Four years after Isis ended, Aaron Turner was living on Vashon Island in Puget Sound, running the SIGE label with his wife Faith Coloccia and writing riffs meant to be the heaviest he'd ever made. What he needed was a drummer who could keep up. Noisey's first headline on the band: heavier than a bag of hammers.

q: a pretty dense, heavy experience and kind of out there
years.h: Kurt Ballou sets Aaron Turner up with Nick Yacyshyn
years.p: [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]'s [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]], who had produced [[Baptists|d00125a6-a009-4171-8cc5-9837620ec200]]' Bloodmines, points Aaron Turner to that band's Vancouver drummer, Nick Yacyshyn. They jam in Vancouver, then Yacyshyn goes to Turner's home on Vashon.
years.xp: Yacyshyn told Exclaim! the music was dense, heavy and out there, and that the pair didn't take other rock bands as their models. Turner insisted it was a fully functional band, not a side project.

years.h: Brian Cook of Russian Circles and Botch comes in on bass
years.p: Exclaim! announces SUMAC with [[Brian Cook|e5915350-afd0-405b-a461-f9c9420f9509]] of [[Russian Circles|cca40a67-e959-46f8-a3f3-8a3f77d2da9e]] and [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] on bass. He was hired to play on the debut and quickly became a full member.

years.h: First show: opening for Deafheaven after two jams
years.p: SUMAC play their first show in December 2014, opening for [[Deafheaven|f4ccf6c5-ad41-4f8f-bb9e-6e2c6ad23302]] in Vancouver. By Wikipedia's account the band had only jammed twice before.

years.h: Rolling Stone crowns Yacyshyn Dave Grohl's favorite new drummer
years.p: Rolling Stone premieres SUMAC's Blight's End Angel under a headline calling Nick Yacyshyn [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]]'s favorite new drummer.
SUMAC's six-song debut, recorded in Seattle by Mell Dettmer ([[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]], Earth) and mastered by Kurt Ballou. Aaron Turner's own SIGE label handles the vinyl.
years.xp: Profound Lore released it on February 17, 2015, after Thorn in the Lion's Paw and Blight's End Angel went out as previews. A short North American tour followed in March.

eras.title: Thrill Jockey, and a meeting with Keiji Haino
eras.text: Signing to Thrill Jockey put SUMAC next to experimental rock rather than metal, and they used the room. Kurt Ballou recorded the albums, and unrehearsed sessions in Tokyo with Japanese noise figure Keiji Haino changed how they wrote.

years.p: Exclaim! reports SUMAC have signed to Chicago's Thrill Jockey for their second album.
Kurt Ballou records SUMAC's second album. Five long tracks, built around Aaron Turner's own struggles with anxiety and what happens when identity comes apart.
Kevin Drumm, [[Endon|92e57202-8ca1-4a5a-9cd9-320a1787de0a]], Samuel Kerridge and Bleed Turquoise remake material from What One Becomes on a four-track SUMAC EP.

years.h: SUMAC and Keiji Haino record in Tokyo, unrehearsed
years.p: In summer 2017 SUMAC record with Japanese noise musician Keiji Haino at Goksound in Tokyo, in sessions Thrill Jockey called completely unrehearsed and non-premeditated.
years.xp: The results became American Dollar Bill – Keep Facing Sideways, You're Too Hideous to Look at Face On, and Thrill Jockey credits the Haino sessions with pushing improvisation into SUMAC's own records from then on. Two more albums with Haino followed.

years.h: A 200-copy tape from a WFMU session
years.p: SIGE releases WFMU Live, a SUMAC cassette recorded for Brian Turner's show on the New Jersey freeform station WFMU, limited to 200 copies.
Thrill Jockey releases the first SUMAC and Keiji Haino album, recorded at Goksound in Tokyo the summer before.

years.h: Love in Shadow · four songs, over an hour
years.p: SUMAC record live over five days at Robert Lang Studios in Shoreline, Washington, with Kurt Ballou. Aaron Turner wanted to write about love in its spiritual, vulnerable sense, and its corrupted forms.
years.xp: Turner's statement for the album complained that rock mostly treats love as heartbreak, idealized romance or a cover for sexual conquest. The four tracks cover jealousy, obsession and addiction as well as devotion.

eras.title: Held, healed, filmed
eras.text: SUMAC kept both tracks running: more Haino albums, and their own records that got longer and looser. Turner's lyrics turned to fatherhood and a society he saw coming apart, and in 2025 they handed the microphone to Moor Mother.

years.h: Second album with Keiji Haino · Trost
years.p: The second SUMAC and Keiji Haino album comes out on Trost Records, on CD in June 2019 and vinyl in July.

years.h: A Sub Pop single and a Saint Vitus live album
years.p: SUMAC release Two Beasts through Sub Pop and, on SIGE, St Vitus 09/07/2018, a live set from the Brooklyn club.

years.h: May You Be Held · three studios, one island
years.p: Recorded with Kurt Ballou in Shoreline, Matt Bayles in Anacortes, and at Aaron Turner's House of Low Culture on Vashon Island. Turner wrote about fatherhood and a society in upheaval.
years.xp: The five tracks open on improvised guitar drones and vibraphone and close on a quiet improvisation. Turner said an artist had to absorb and interpret a time of upheaval, and called the record a reminder of the life force that binds people together.

years.h: Third album with Keiji Haino · Thrill Jockey
years.p: SUMAC and Keiji Haino's third album together, on Thrill Jockey.
SUMAC's fifth studio album, Thrill Jockey catalog number 609: four long pieces about wounds as a way to growth. The Keeper's Tongue EP followed the same year.

years.cap: The Film by SUMAC and Moor Mother (Thrill Jockey, 2025)
years.p: SUMAC make a double album with Philadelphia poet and musician [[Moor Mother|16610cf1-5ed5-4770-89b4-bf7e7aca7ebf]] at Studio Litho in Seattle, with singers Kyle Kidd, Sovie and Candice Hoyes. Aaron Turner painted the art.
years.xp: Moor Mother framed it as a work of art to be taken whole, like a film, not a set of songs. Its themes, in her words, include land, displacement, the climate, human rights, war and peace.
